# Fixtures where the SELF-HOST x86-64 path disagrees with the native compiler.
#
# Format: <fixture-name> <#issue> <reason>
#
# Same contract as selfhost-wasm-known-divergences.txt: TestFernFixturesSelfHostX86_64
# lists these rather than skipping them, so the lane is green with them listed, a
# NEW divergence fails, and a listed fixture that starts PASSING also fails — an
# allowlist nobody prunes is where bugs go to be forgotten.
#
# Two rules for adding a row, both learned from the wasm leg's first run (which
# reported 26 mismatches, 14 of them harness artifacts):
#
#   1. Reproduce the value before writing it down, and record the measured
#      self-host and native figures in the reason.
#   2. Rule out the harness's `import "core/int"` injection first. The native
#      legs inject that import into the entry file (LoadCheckMono, for wasmbin's
#      PrintMainResult); the self-host CLI injects nothing. A compile failure
#      naming a missing method is that asymmetry, not a compiler divergence.
#
# Unlike the wasm leg, this one has no exit-code blind spot: a native binary
# carries main's return over the full 0..255, so every fixture's VALUE is
# checked. That is why the six #6049 regex rows lived here at all — they expect
# >= 126, so the wasm leg only ever logged "exit value unmeasurable" for them.
#
# All 16 were measured on the first two runs (49e762e0, d67de908), 317 fixtures
# run. Fifteen have since been FIXED — `eq_struct_enum` + `ord_struct_enum`
# (#6009), `tuple_match_expr` (#6010), `int_wrap` + `u64_max_to_f64_is_huge`
# (#6050 / #6051), `multiline_stdin` (#6052), `pure_collection_aliases` +
# `map_struct_value_field` (the #6007 slices), `derive_json` (#6009, two
# separate bugs — see the notes in the wasm sibling), the six regex
# fixtures (#6049) and `generic_method_typeparams` (#6007). NONE remains.
#
# The #6049 six were recorded as "hangs (killed at 20s, no output)", which by the
# time they were diagnosed was stale: they SEGV'd in milliseconds on unbounded
# recursion through a parse tree that had become self-referential. Two rc bugs,
# both in irlower: a direct ENUM struct field read stored into a container took
# no Perceus dup against the per-type __struct_drop helper's k_enum dec, and a
# match arm's payload ARRAY binding was swept at every exit though the enum (or
# Option/Result) box owns the buffer. Recording a symptom without re-measuring it
# is how a stack-exhaustion SEGV gets hunted as an infinite loop.

# --- IR-ineligible, hard error since #3457 deleted the AST emitters ---------
# The leg re-runs these under FERN_STRICT_IR=1 and logs the named bail site.
# All three of the original are FIXED: `pure_collection_aliases` (its bail named
# `Map.cleared`, which had no lowering at all), `map_struct_value_field` (an
# `it.value().field` with no struct recovery) — see the wasm sibling's notes —
# and `generic_method_typeparams`, whose `Box[T].map[U]` left the method's own
# type param free in the receiver clone, so the return mangled to a `Box__U`
# nothing generated. Generic-struct methods with their own type params now ride
# the free-generic fold (`__smm_<Base>_<name>`), like the array + map methods.
#
# The list is EMPTY. Keep the contract in force rather than deleting the file:
# an empty allowlist is what makes the NEXT divergence fail the leg.

# --- new, first seen on x86-64: ALL THREE NOW FIXED ------------------------
# `int_wrap` (#6050) and `u64_max_to_f64_is_huge` (#6051): the i32 formatter now
# carries its magnitude unsigned (so INT_MIN's self-negation still renders its
# digits), and int→f64 is emitted per the op's width + signedness (so a u64
# >= 2^63 stops converting as -1.0).
#
# `multiline_stdin` (#6052): read_line issued one read(0, buf, 256) and threw
# away every byte after the first newline, so a read-until-EOF loop got one line
# and then a genuine EOF. It reads a byte at a time now, like native. This was
# never x86-64-specific — all three self-host backends had the same single-read
# shape, and the wasm leg only looked clean because it sets skipStdin and so
# never asked. Keep that in mind before reading a lane's silence as coverage.

# --- fresh-owned-container read: not reclaimed by the self-host ------------
# `alloc_flat_index_of_fresh_container` reports the allocator's fresh-byte
# SHAPE for a value read out of a container nothing names (`mk()[i]`,
# `mk().field`). Native reclaims the container at the read; the self-host does
# not, on any of its three legs.
#
#     got:  8361 / 16762 / grows
#     want: 8361 / 16762 / flat
#
# The two VALUES agree — the self-host computes the right answer and simply
# never reclaims. Split and run through the self-host CLI, both halves diverge:
# the index shape reads 4181 / 8382 / grows and the field shape 4180 / 8380 /
# grows, so this is one missing mechanism rather than two coincidences.
#
# Native pairs a retain of the loaded value with an is_unique-gated deep drop of
# the container — the value aliases the buffer being freed, so a plain drop
# would be a use-after-free. The self-host sources carry none of that machinery
# (no __arr_idx / fresh_owned / owned_call_result anywhere in
# examples/self_host), which is the RECLAIM half docs/RC-PERCEUS-SELF-HOST-PORT.md
# still has open. Tracked as #6491.
#
# Worth knowing while porting: the sibling `alloc_flat_under_reclaim` PASSES
# here. That case lets the whole allocation die, which the self-host handles;
# this one keeps the element alive while the container dies, which it does not.
alloc_flat_index_of_fresh_container 6491 self-host: a container read at `mk()[i]` / `mk().field` is never reclaimed — grows, native flat

# --- array-store element: the move is not ported ---------------------------
# `alloc_flat_array_push_bound_elem` reports the allocator's fresh-byte SHAPE
# for an element BOUND to a local before being pushed — `var v = …;
# xs = xs.append(v)` — against the same value pushed inline.
#
#     got:  3700 / 7400 / grows
#     want: 3700 / 7400 / flat
#
# The two VALUES agree, so this is the #6491 signature again: the self-host
# computes the right answer and never reclaims.
#
# Native treats the element as a MOVE when it is an owned rc local at its last
# use — the retain is skipped and the buffer's deep drop is the single release
# (#6532). Before that the element took BOTH a retain and an escape taint, and
# the taint suppressed the balancing release. The self-host has neither half:
# nothing in examples/self_host corresponds to markConstructionMoves / moveSites
# for an array store, so the element keeps its retain and nothing gives it back.
#
# The case covers two shapes deliberately, and a partial port will still fail
# it: the direct `xs.append(v)`, and the push nested in a struct literal's field
# (`d = Doc { ...d, vals: d.vals.append(v) }`), which native missed until the
# move walk learned to descend into container operands. Tracked as #6535.
alloc_flat_array_push_bound_elem 6535 self-host: a bound array-store element keeps its retain and is never released — grows, native flat
